prerequisites: Having previously taken Physics II (2nd semester of 1st year, plan 2020)

learning_outcomes.text: Provide a solid scientific basis to understand and study the equilibrium and/or movement of mechanisms.
Familiarize students with mathematical modeling in mechanical engineering.
Acquire proficiency in using mathematical knowledge for solving technical problems.
Develop a critical spirit in solving problems in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Field of velocities in rigid bodies.
Field of accelerations in rigid bodies.
Absolute and relative motion of a material point (velocity and acceleration).
Relative motion between two rigid bodies.
Pole velocity and pole changing velocity.
Definitions and relationships between moments of inertia.
Calculation of moment of inertia with respect to an axis.
Moments and principle axis of intertia.
Equations of the Statics of a material system.
Friction to relative sliding: Coulomb hypothesis.
Mechanical work: conservative forces and potential function.
Work of interior and exterior forces acting on a rigid body.
Application to the study of equilibrium of mechanical systems.
Kinetic system: linear and angular moments and Kinetic energy.
Calculation of the angular moment in a point (body with fixed point and free body).
Calculation of Kinetic energy (body with fixed point and free body).
Equations of movement based on Newtonian Mechanics.
teaching_methods: Student study based on different information sources
Personal interviews with the course professor (addressing doubts)
assessment_rules: The ordinary examination consists of a partial exam (25%) and a mandatory final exam (75%). The partial exam can be released if a grade of 50% or higher is obtained, otherwise its content must be re-evaluated during the final exam. An optional exercise can add up to 1 extra point to the final grade if it exceeds 4.0. For the extraordinary examination, the partial exam grade is retained if released, and any extra points from the optional exercise are also kept, but no other approved parts from the ordinary final exam are carried over.
